title: How Sam Altman built OpenAI: conviction on one bet, speed, and still building a real business
summary: Sam Altman tells Garry Tan how OpenAI began with a narrow bet on deep learning and scaling, why extreme conviction must be paired with truth-seeking, and why this is the best time yet to start a company. His startup advice: bet on the AI trend, move at the speed of the technology, and still build a real business.

principles.text: With fewer resources than rivals, pick one bet and concentrate fully instead of spreading across many.
principles.quote: they're going to try a lot of things and we've just got to pick one and really concentrate. And that's how we can win here

principles.text: Run on conviction only until data arrives, then follow the data. Conviction without truth-seeking is ineffective.
principles.quote: Conviction is great until the moment you have data one way or the other. And there are a lot of people who hold on past the moment of data.

principles.text: Platform shifts are when upstarts have their edge; big companies win when things move slowly.
principles.quote: Big companies have the edge when things are like moving slowly and not that dynamic. And then when something like this or mobile or the internet or semiconductor revolution happens

principles.text: A startup's top edge is speed, focus and conviction. Build the day you see a new capability, not in a quarterly plan.
principles.quote: your advantage with speed and focus and conviction and the ability to react to to how fast the technology is moving that is that is the number one edge of a startup kind of ever but especially right now

principles.text: New technology doesn't exempt you from business fundamentals. Demos are easy; a real business is the goal.
principles.quote: But building a business, man, that's the brass ring. The rules still apply. You can do it faster than ever before and better than ever before, but you still have to build a business.

principles.text: Peer pressure is unavoidable, so choose your peer group deliberately and early.
principles.quote: no one is immune to peer pressure and so all you can do is like pick good peers.
